newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus to buy western combines instead of Russian.
newsitem.headline: Belarus to buy western combines instead of Russian.

text.p: Belarus Agriculture Minister Vasily Leonov said on Thursday Minsk refused to buy Russian-made combines and planned to purchase German-made harvesters.
Leonov also said that the reason was the postponment by the Russian government the allocation of the 500 billion Russian roubles credit for the purchase of Russian-made Don combines.

"Belarus will change its orientation towards European combines, which are technically better and use less fuel," Leonov told a news conference. "This will allow to reach next year a completely new level in grain production next year."
Leonov said Belarus would buy 3,000 German-made Class and MDW combines on a five-year credit with 10 percent intrest through Belinterfinans company, controlled by state-owned Belvneshekonombank.
Belarus plans to harvest this year 6.4 million tonnes of grain compared to 5.4 million tonnes last year. --Larisa Sayenko, Minsk bureau +7 017 227 3594
